vote_record.summary: The House passed a concurrent resolution directing the President to withdraw U.S. armed forces from hostilities with Iran under the War Powers Resolution.
The resolution directed the President, under the War Powers Resolution, to withdraw U.S. armed forces from hostilities with Iran.
The amendment would prohibit all U.S. security assistance funding for Ukraine, except for embassy security, effectively cutting aid; it failed with 76 yeas and 349 nays.

The amendment would bar the Department of Defense from using taxpayer money to cover costs of foreign military personnel participating in bilateral or multilateral exercises with the United States unless a waiver is granted, and the amendment was defeated.

The House passed the FY2027 National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, allocating roughly $61 billion for national security and foreign assistance, including continued military aid to allies such as Israel and Ukraine.
The motion to recommit sought to strip the FY 2027 National Security appropriations bill of its foreign military assistance provisions, removing billions of dollars in aid for Ukraine and Israel.

Amendment would prohibit using appropriated funds for Jordan, cutting $2.1 billion from the National Security Investment Programs, Foreign Military Financing, Global Health Programs and related accounts.
Amendment would prohibit the use of appropriated funds for Israel, cutting $3.3 billion from the Foreign Military Financing program.
The resolution directed the President, under the War Powers Resolution, to remove U.S. armed forces from hostilities in Lebanon; it failed with 189 yeas and 213 nays.
The House passed the Ukraine Support Act, authorizing about $30 billion in additional military assistance to Ukraine, including weapons, ammunition, and training.
The resolution directed the President, under the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States armed forces deployed in Lebanon.
The House voted to discharge H.R. 2913, authorizing roughly $14.5 billion in additional military and economic assistance for Ukraine.
The House passed a concurrent resolution directing the President to withdraw U.S. armed forces from hostilities with Iran under the War Powers Resolution, voting 215‑208.

The amendment would have redirected $481,832,000 from the NATO Security Investment Program to the Military Construction, Defense‑Wide account, cutting foreign military financing for NATO; the amendment failed.
The resolution would have directed the President to withdraw U.S. armed forces from hostilities against Iran under the War Powers Resolution, but it failed as the House voted 212‑210 against it.
The resolution directed the President to withdraw U.S. armed forces from hostilities with Iran under the War Powers Resolution; it failed 213‑213.
The House voted on a concurrent resolution directing the President to withdraw U.S. forces from unauthorized hostilities in Iran under the War Powers Resolution; the measure failed 212‑217.
The resolution would have directed the removal of United States armed forces from Venezuela that were deployed without congressional authorization.
The House voted on H CON RES 64 to direct the removal of U.S. armed forces from hostilities in Venezuela that lack congressional authorization; the resolution failed 211‑213.

The resolution would have required the President to withdraw U.S. armed forces from hostilities with presidentially designated terrorist organizations in the Western Hemisphere, but it failed to pass.

The amendment would prohibit all U.S. security assistance funding for Ukraine, except for embassy security, effectively cutting aid; it failed with 76 yeas and 349 nays.

The amendment would bar the Department of Defense from using taxpayer money to cover costs of foreign military personnel participating in bilateral or multilateral exercises with the United States unless a waiver is granted, and the amendment was defeated.

The House passed the FY2027 National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, allocating roughly $61 billion for national security and foreign assistance, including continued military aid to allies such as Israel and Ukraine.

Amendment would prohibit using appropriated funds for Jordan, cutting $2.1 billion from the National Security Investment Programs, Foreign Military Financing, Global Health Programs and related accounts.

The resolution directed the President, under the War Powers Resolution, to remove U.S. armed forces from hostilities in Lebanon; it failed with 189 yeas and 213 nays.

The resolution would have directed the President to withdraw U.S. armed forces from hostilities against Iran under the War Powers Resolution, but it failed as the House voted 212‑210 against it.

The House voted on a concurrent resolution directing the President to withdraw U.S. forces from unauthorized hostilities in Iran under the War Powers Resolution; the measure failed 212‑217.

The Protect Taiwan Act authorizes increased U.S. security assistance for Taiwan, directing the President to provide additional military aid (approximately $500 million) and develop a strategy to deter Chinese aggression.
The resolution would have directed the removal of United States armed forces from Venezuela that were deployed without congressional authorization.

The resolution would have required the President to withdraw U.S. armed forces from hostilities with presidentially designated terrorist organizations in the Western Hemisphere, but it failed to pass.

FEC:H8MO01143.description: Cori Anika Bush is an American politician, nurse, pastor, and Black Lives Matter activist who served as the U.S. representative for Missouri's 1st congressional district from 2021 to 2025. She is a member of the Democratic Party and the Democratic Socialists of America.

FEC:H8NH01186.name: Maura Sullivan
FEC:H8NH01186.description: Maura C. Sullivan is an American politician and former government official. Sullivan previously served as an official in the Obama administration from 2014 to 2016 in both the United States Department of Veterans Affairs and the United States Department of Defense. She also served on the American Battle Monuments Commission starting in 2010, and began her career as an officer in the United States Marine Corps serving in the Iraq War after the September 11 attacks.

FEC:H8TX32098.name: Colin Allred
FEC:H8TX32098.description: Colin Zachary Allred is an American politician, civil rights lawyer, and former professional football player who served as the U.S. representative for Texas's 32nd congressional district from 2019 to 2025. The district included the northeastern corner of Dallas as well as many of its northeastern suburbs. He is a member of the Democratic Party, and is its nominee for the 33rd congressional district in 2026.

FEC:H8VA05106.name: Thomas Perriello

FEC:S0KY00339.name: Amy McGrath

She was inspired to be a fighter pilot after studying World War II aviation in middle school and taking family trips to Wright-Patterson Air Force Base. During her 20 years of service in the Marine Corps, McGrath flew 89 combat missions against al-Qaeda and the Taliban.

FEC:S6MI00418.name: Abdul El-Sayed
FEC:S6MI00418.description: Abdul El-Sayed is an American epidemiologist, public health administrator, academic and politician who is the Democratic nominee in the 2026 United States Senate election in Michigan.

FEC:S6MS00133.name: Scott Colom
FEC:S6MS00133.description: Scott Winston Colom is an American lawyer and politician serving as district attorney for the 16th Judicial District of Mississippi. He is the Democratic nominee in the 2026 United States Senate election in Mississippi. He is a former nominee to serve as a United States district judge of the United States District Court for the Northern District of Mississippi.

FEC:S6MT00295.name: Kurt Alme
FEC:S6MT00295.description: Kurt Gordon Alme is an American attorney who served from March 2025 to March 2026 as the United States attorney for the District of Montana. He resigned to run in the 2026 United States Senate election in Montana. He is the Republican nominee in the election.

FEC:S6NC00340.name: Wiley Nickel
FEC:S6NC00340.description: George Wilmarth "Wiley" Nickel III is an American attorney and Democratic politician who served as the U.S. representative for North Carolina's 13th congressional district from 2023 to 2025.

FEC:S6NC00407.name: Roy Cooper
FEC:S6NC00407.description: Roy Asberry Cooper III is an American politician and lawyer who served as the 75th governor of North Carolina from 2017 to 2025. A member of the Democratic Party, he previously served as the 50th attorney general of North Carolina from 2001 to 2017 and in the North Carolina General Assembly from 1987 to 2001.

FEC:S6NC00415.name: Michael Whatley
FEC:S6NC00415.description: Michael David Whatley is an American politician and lawyer who was chair of the Republican National Committee from 2024 to 2025. He previously served as chair of the North Carolina Republican Party from 2019 to 2024.

FEC:S6OH00163.name: Sherrod Brown
FEC:S6OH00163.description: Sherrod Campbell Brown is an American politician who served from 2007 to 2025 as a United States senator from Ohio. Previously, he served in the Ohio House of Representatives from 1975 to 1983, was Ohio secretary of state from 1983 to 1991, and was the U.S. representative for Ohio's 13th congressional district from 1993 to 2007. He is a member of the Democratic Party, and has been described as a populist.

FEC:S6SC04296.name: Paul Dans
FEC:S6SC04296.description: Paul Edouard Dans is an American lawyer, political operative and politician, who briefly served as Chief of Staff to the Office of Personnel Management in President Trump's first administration. A Republican, he is best known for leading Project 2025, the Heritage Foundation's 2025 presidential transition project intended to enact conservative policy through the federal government. Prior to entering politics, Dans was a lawyer.

FEC:S6TX00388.name: Warren Paxton
FEC:S6TX00388.description: Warren Kenneth Paxton Jr. is an American politician and lawyer who has served as the 51st attorney general of Texas since 2015. He is the Republican Party nominee in the 2026 United States Senate election in Texas.

FEC:S6TX00479.name: James Talarico
FEC:S6TX00479.description: James Dell Talarico is an American politician, Presbyterian seminarian, and educator serving since 2018 as a member of the Texas House of Representatives. He is the Democratic nominee in the 2026 U.S. Senate election in Texas.

FEC:S8VA00321.name: Bert Mizusawa
FEC:S8VA00321.description: Bert Kameaaloha Mizusawa is a retired major general in the United States Army, serving in the Army from 1979 to 2015. Mizusawa also served in the United States Senate as a professional staff member and as a Senior Executive in the Pentagon, making him one of only a handful of individuals to serve at flag rank in the military as well as in both the legislative and executive branches. Mizusawa is also an attorney and is admitted to the bars of New York, the District of Columbia, Virginia and the United States Supreme Court. He is the Republican nominee for the 2026 United States Senate election

TR:becca balint|.name: Becca Balint
TR:becca balint|.description: Rebecca A. Balint is an American politician who is a member of the United States House of Representatives from Vermont's at-large congressional district as a member of the Democratic Party. She served as a member of the Vermont Senate from Windham County from 2015 to 2023, as majority leader from 2017 to 2021, and as president pro tempore from 2021 to 2023.

TR:catherine cortezmasto|NV.name: Catherine Cortez-Masto
TR:catherine cortezmasto|NV.description: Catherine Marie Cortez Masto is an American lawyer and politician serving as the senior United States senator from Nevada, a seat she has held since 2017. A member of the Democratic Party, Cortez Masto served as the 32nd attorney general of Nevada from 2007 to 2015.

TR:chuck fleischmann|.name: Chuck Fleischmann
TR:chuck fleischmann|.description: Charles Joseph Fleischmann is an American attorney and politician who has been the U.S. representative for Tennessee's 3rd congressional district since 2011. The district is based in Chattanooga and includes a large part of East Tennessee, including Oak Ridge. He is a member of the Republican Party.

TR:debbie wassermanschultz|FL.name: Debbie Wasserman-Schultz
TR:debbie wassermanschultz|FL.description: Deborah Wasserman Schultz is an American politician serving as the U.S. representative for Florida's 25th congressional district, first elected to Congress in 2004. A member of the Democratic Party, she was the chair of the Democratic National Committee (DNC) from 2011 until her resignation in 2016.

TR:dusty johnson|.name: Dusty Johnson
TR:dusty johnson|.description: Dustin Michael Johnson is an American politician serving as the U.S. representative for South Dakota's at-large congressional district since 2019. A member of the Republican Party, he served as South Dakota Public Utilities Commissioner from 2005 to 2011, when he was appointed chief of staff to Governor Dennis Daugaard, a position he held until 2014. Between his state political career and congressional service, Johnson was the vice-president of Vantage Point Solutions in Mitchell, South Dakota.

TR:harriet hageman|.name: Harriet Hageman
TR:harriet hageman|.description: Harriet Maxine Hageman is an American politician and attorney serving as the U.S. representative for Wyoming's at-large congressional district since 2023. She is the Republican nominee for the 2026 United States Senate election in Wyoming, seeking to succeed incumbent Cynthia Lummis.

TR:julie fedorchak|.name: Julie Fedorchak
TR:julie fedorchak|.description: Julie Ann Fedorchak is an American politician serving as the U.S. representative for North Dakota's at-large congressional district since 2025. Previously, she served on the North Dakota Public Service Commission from 2012 to 2025 after being appointed by Governor Jack Dalrymple.

TR:lamonica mciver|.name: LaMonica McIver
TR:lamonica mciver|.description: LaMonica R. McIver is an American politician serving as the U.S. representative for New Jersey's 10th congressional district since 2024. A member of the Democratic Party, she served on the Newark municipal council from 2018 to 2024. McIver was first elected to Congress in a September 2024 special election to succeed Donald Payne Jr. in Congress, who died in office in April.

TR:sarah mcbride|.name: Sarah McBride
TR:sarah mcbride|.description: Sarah Elizabeth McBride is an American politician, author, and LGBTQ rights activist serving as the U.S. representative for Delaware's at-large congressional district since 2025. A member of the Democratic Party, she served in the Delaware Senate from 2021 to 2025, representing the 1st district. Prior, she was the national press secretary of the Human Rights Campaign from 2016 to 2021. McBride is the nation's highest ranking openly transgender elected official and the first openly transgender member of the United States Congress. TR:wesley bell|.name: Wesley Bell
TR:wesley bell|.description: Wesley Jonell-Cleavon Bell is an American attorney and politician serving as the U.S. representative for Missouri's 1st congressional district, based in St. Louis, since 2025. A member of the Democratic Party, he previously served as prosecuting attorney for St. Louis County, Missouri, from 2019 to 2025.
